messages:
maria: quick thought — can we avoid a heavy active/active refactor by pushing a small residency decision layer into the edge proxy? keep runtime unchanged, let proxy attach enforcement headers and take routing decisions.
sam: like an 'X-Resident-Region' header?
maria: exactly. control plane sets it per-tenant. proxy consults capacity + policy, routes to resident region or applies fallback. minimal runtime changes.
jordan: nice for rollout speed. concerns: proxy becomes the policy surface and we still need consistent KV ownership hints so caches don't diverge.
lee: agree. also write coordination is tricky. who holds the lease when proxy forwards to non-resident execution? cross-region lease swaps are expensive.
maria: sketched two modes: 

1) proxy-prefer-local
- proxy tries to hit resident region if healthy.
- if resident overloaded, fallback per tenant policy: nearest-compatible or read-only degrade.
- runtime lease semantics unchanged — lease swaps happen if runtime needs them.

2) proxy-escrow-intent
- proxy forwards a thin intent to resident runtime which issues a short-lived execution token.
- non-resident execution can run the op with that token without swapping leases every time.
- trades protocol complexity for fewer lease handoffs.

sam: escrow seems safer for correctness but requires new token flow + audit trails.
sophia: cache invalidation question — when routing differs caches will be stale. propose tenant-level cache version header so proxy can force bypass when stale.
jordan: +1. also add a soft-evict marker so resident nodes flag items as 'stale-due-routing' rather than immediate purge. helps warm-ups.
lee: observability needs — we must tag cost & latency when fallback occurs so billing and SLOs align.
maria: propose headers:
```
X-Resident-Region: eu-west-1
X-Residency-Policy: strict|preferred|allow-fallback
X-Cache-Version: 42
X-Route-Trace-Id: rtr_abc123
```

sophia: clarify semantics: strict = deny if not resident? how to handle emergency SLA failovers?
maria: strict => fail with policy error. emergency overrides require ops/legal gate, either manual or an automated high-severity signal. keep default conservative.
sam: rollout plan idea:
- phase 0: header only, telemetry-only at proxy (no enforcement) for 2 weeks.
- phase 1: preferred enforcement, honor resident when available, fallback allowed. add cache-version awareness + billing tags.
- phase 2: enable strict, experiment with escrow tokens for write optimization.
jordan: telemetry we need in phase 0:
- percent resident vs fallback
- latency/error delta for fallback paths
- KV cache hit rate split by tenant & region
- count of lease swaps triggered by proxy routing

lee: perf: header check must stay in fast path, no blocking I/O. should be tiny CPU cost.
sophia: compliance: emit an event whenever a request crosses residency boundary, include tenant id and route-trace-id. we need this for audits.
infra-bot: deploy-checks: config flag residency.enforce=false exists in staging. integration tests in tests/residency/ validate headers + cache-version.
maria: next steps — I'll open a short PR with header schema, proxy decision matrix, and a telemetry dashboard mock. please review when I post. :eyes:
sam: I'll focus on billing/tagging details.
jordan: I'll prototype cache-version handling and soft-evict marker.
lee: I'll analyze lease-swap load and whether escrow tokens avoid most swaps.
sophia: I'll draft compliance event schema and the emergency override runbook.
maria: thanks all, moving these action items into the RFC follow-up doc.
